competencyAxisExtraction.defect: The first extraction paired labels to D01-D12 by position after dropping only lines that matched an id exactly. The archive renders the matrix as two column streams that pdftotext offsets by two rows, so the header line and every embedded id survived into the label text and the pairing was wrong for every row. Found independently by DEVICE-02 and recorded as B9.
competencyAxisExtraction.method: Columns are split at the measured boundary (column 31), each stream's header cells are dropped by name, and the two streams are paired in order. The extractor refuses to emit unless both streams are exactly twelve entries, the ids are a contiguous D01-D12, and no label carries an embedded id, three-or-more-space column bleed, or a header cell.
competencyAxisExtraction.pairingEvidence: Same-row pairing would orphan two labels and leave two ids unlabelled, which cannot be the intent of a declared twelve-axis matrix. The corpus then settles it empirically: records tagged KB-D10 carry privacyFlags at 47% against an 11-17% baseline for all eleven other axes, and stream-order pairing is what puts 'HIPAA, privacy, security, and minimum necessary' at D10. Same-row pairing would put it at D09, which sits at baseline (11%).
